messages:
marta: heads up - customer acme-finance-prod started seeing intermittent 401s on /v1/generate around 2025-11-03T08:10:21Z. They attached this response body: {\"error\":\"invalid_signature\",\"detail\":\"kid not found\"}. Noticed right after we rolled a model and rotated signing keys on their SSO path.

jordan: which auth path are they using? api-key or OIDC/SAML token exchange?

marta: OIDC bearer from our auth-proxy (company SSO via Okta). Tokens are service-to-service, JWT signed by acme's IdP.

kev: digging into the runtime logs for that customer. Saw repeated lines like: 
```
2025-11-03T08:09:58Z runtime-auth ERROR jwt: no matching key for kid=9f1c3a
2025-11-03T08:10:03Z runtime-auth WARN jwks: using cached jwks (age=21420s)
2025-11-03T08:10:21Z runtime-auth ERROR verify: token invalid_signature
```
Looks like our JWKS cache was stale (cache TTL configured to 6h) while their IdP rotated keys and returned Cache-Control: max-age=300. We were ignoring cache headers.

sam: confirmed the jwks endpoint returned a new key and Cache-Control: max-age=300. example request: 
```
curl -i https://acme-okta.example/.well-known/jwks.json
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: max-age=300, must-revalidate
Content-Type: application/json

{\"keys\":[{\"kid\":\"ab23...\",\"kty\":\"RSA\",...}, {\"kid\":\"9f1c3a\",\"kty\":\"RSA\",...}]}
```

kev: reproduction steps I used locally:
1) fetch old jwks and seed runtime cache
2) rotate keys on a minimal IdP (script attached)
3) issue token signed with new kid
4) call /v1/generate with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> 401 invalid_signature or \"kid not found\" 

Example curl showing failure: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
> Content-Type: application/json
{ \"error\": \"unauthenticated\", \"message\": \"invalid_signature: kid 0x9f1c3a not in jwks\" }
```

marta: the customer reported it was intermittent: sometimes requests succeed after a short window. Could that be clock skew?

kev: clock skew is separate but worth checking. I did see some \"token not yet valid\" in other traces: 
```
verify error: token nbf 2025-11-03T08:11:00Z (client clock ahead by 120s)
```
So two orthogonal issues: 1) JWKS cache ignoring Cache-Control/ETag -> stale keys, 2) small client clock skew causing nbf/iat rejections.

jordan: what was ops mitigation we gave the customer?

marta: opsbot executed a one-off jwks refresh for that customer and asked them to retry. opsbot status below.

opsbot: POST /internal/admin/jwks/refresh?tenant=acme-finance-prod -> 200 OK
opsbot: cache cleared for tenant=acme-finance-prod, forced fetch from https://acme-okta.example/.well-known/jwks.json

marta: customer retried ~2m later and reported success. They also tightened their IdP rotation window.

kev: proposed long-term fixes: 
- Respect Cache-Control and ETag headers from JWKS endpoints and set cache TTL accordingly.
- On 401 with \"kid not found\", trigger a synchronous JWKS refetch once (race-safe) before rejecting.
- Add configurable skew (default +2m) for JWT `nbf`/`iat` checks to tolerate small clock drift.
- Add a monitoring alert when jwks fetch returns different key set (key churn) more than X times per hour.

sam: +1. Also add unit/integration tests: simulate jwks rotation + request flood to ensure refetch logic doesn't thundering-herd.

qa-bot: created ticket RED-4012 in infra-auth with repro script and logs. Steps included, label = p0 until patch is deployed.

kev: quick patch notes I pushed: 
```
- runtime/auth/jwks_manager.go: respect Cache-Control max-age and ETag
- runtime/auth/verify.go: on ErrKidNotFound -> jwksManager.FetchIfStale(ctx) then retry once
- runtime/auth/clock.go: allow configurable skew (defaultSeconds=120)
```
PR: https://git.redwood/infraruntime/pulls/1287 (in review by eng-runtime).

marta: customer-facing text we used to update support ticket: 
\"We observed your IdP rotated signing keys and our JWKS cache had an extended TTL. We cleared the cache and added a temporary tolerance for clock skew. We'll deploy a fix to honor JWKS cache headers and retry fetch on kid-mismatch to prevent recurrence. Please confirm if you still see failures after 1 hour.\"

jordan: have we checked for any other tenants hitting the same pattern?

kev: grepped logs for \"no matching key for kid\" across prod -> found 7 tenants in last 24h, most transient. Filing followups.

marta: remaining action items:
- eng-runtime deploy PR and smoke test (kev)
- add alert for jwks-churn (sam)
- update runbook to include forced jwks refresh endpoint and how to ask ops to clear (marta)
- customer follow-up scheduled (jordan)

opsbot: scheduled canary deploy of PR 1287 to us-east-1 at 2025-11-03T20:00:00Z (ETA 30m).

marta: thanks all — closing thread once deploy green and customer confirms.
